title: This Ant Sprints Across Scorching Sahara Sand at 108 Body Lengths a Second
subject: silver ant

scenes.text: The Sahara sand can cook most animals alive. This ant runs across it anyway.
The silver ant has about ten minutes outside its nest before the heat becomes too much.
It sprints at about 108 body lengths per second. A cheetah manages around 16.
That's roughly 0.86 metres per second, the fastest ant ever recorded.
The sand can pass 60 degrees Celsius, so it races to find a dead insect.
Its silver hairs reflect sunlight and help keep the body cool. Speed, plus armour.

description:
The Saharan silver ant runs about 108 body lengths per second across scorching sand, faster than a cheetah relative to size.
It only forages for about ten minutes at a time, and its silver hairs help shed heat.
What's the fastest animal you know for its size?
